source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:math/0410354, author preprint corresponding to Mathematical Methods of Statistics 14 (2005)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies pointwise random-design regression at a vanishing or exploding design density and gives a regularly varying pointwise minimax rate n^{-s/(1+2s+beta)} times a slowly varying factor.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:math/0503715, corresponding to ESAIM: Probability and Statistics 11 (2007), 344–364
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: This is the pointwise degenerate-random-design adaptation paper, with a local-polynomial Lepski selector and a logarithmic adaptive payment; it is not the arXiv identifier or page range listed in the proposal.

The paper studies random-design regression in a minimax framework using a spatially dependent uniform metric for locally vanishing design density, and constructs a design- and smoothness-adaptive estimator.

source_verification_receipts.version: Location-Based Methods preprint, accessed as the 2025/2026 public version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The location-based BATEC analysis assumes the bivariate score density is continuous and bounded away from zero on its support, while treating pointwise and uniform boundary-curve inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2510.26051v4, 25 May 2026; public version corresponding to the 2026 Journal of Econometrics paper
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies distance-based estimation of the boundary average treatment-effect curve, including pointwise and uniform identification, inference, and minimax lower bounds for a broad class of isotropic regression estimators.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1303.7152v4, corresponding to Annals of Statistics 42 (2014), 1787–1818
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives anti-concentration-based Gaussian multiplier-bootstrap honest bands, including data-selected resolutions, rather than an exact finite-pattern sparse-cell band.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1110.4985v2, corresponding to Electronic Journal of Statistics 6 (2012), 1490–1516
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes self-similarity as necessary and sufficient for adaptive confidence bands over smoothness classes, not for random-design thickness-profile unions.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear regression functionals over convex classes, including regression-discontinuity applications.

The paper is titled “Thin Sets Are Not Equally Thin: Minimax Learning of Submanifold Integrals” and is authored by Xiaohong Chen and Wayne Yuan Gao; it studies minimax-optimal rates for integral functionals on submanifolds.

If retaining flat geometry, prove a genuinely new necessary-and-sufficient observable profile-separation criterion with an explicit computable test, rather than restating the parent’s local-band OEQ.
Correct the Gaiffas and Chen–Gao bibliographic identities and give exact source anchors for every comparator before proposing a replacement kernel.
